name: leopardi3/oecd-cli-equity-returns
what_it_holds: Small research repo testing whether the OECD Composite Leading Indicator predicts equity returns -- ships the pulled OECD CLI series across four markets plus a leakage-free walk-forward backtest harness (stats + ML benchmarks).
why_useful: Doubles as (a) a country-level consumer/business-cycle leading-indicator series for regional demand context and (b) a concrete worked example of a leakage-free, point-in-time-honest backtest design -- relevant to this project's own W1/W2 pre-registration discipline (methods gap #17).

name: gdelt2HeaderRows
what_it_holds: CSV schema/header-row reference files for the GDELT 2.0 Global Knowledge Graph, Events Database, and Event Mentions database (TableId, data type, nullability, description per field). 54 stars, 27 forks, 11 commits.
why_useful: Not a travel-filtered GDELT feed itself, but the schema reference is what a follow-up agent needs to correctly parse GDELT's raw 15-minute event files for travel-relevant CAMEO event codes (protests, disasters, border/visa policy actions, transport strikes) feeding events/shocks work (gap #11) and regulation tracking (gap #12) via GDELT GKG themes.

name: JunchiDu/pead-event-study-us-firms
what_it_holds: R event-study code testing whether post-earnings-announcement drift persists among 50 large US firms, 2000-2024, using CRSP/Compustat data (licensed, not bundled).
why_useful: A ready-made PEAD event-study framework (gap #17 methods) that could be adapted to test whether ABNB (and peers BKNG/EXPE) exhibit drift after beats/misses on nights/ADR/guide -- relevant to how the stock trades in the days after the 5 Nov print, though it requires CRSP/Compustat access we may not have.

name: data
what_it_holds: FiveThirtyEight's full data-and-code repository behind all its published articles and graphics (CC-BY-4.0, 17,445 stars, actively updated through Sep 2026). Includes the uber-tlc-foil-response-style subfolders among many other topic folders (gig economy, freelance/labor-market pieces, consumer spending stories) each with committed CSVs matching the underlying article.
why_useful: A broad, well-maintained pointer repo worth a manual folder-by-folder pass for any gig-economy, freelance-labor, or consumer-spending story with a data release; too large and heterogeneous to fully catalogue in this pass, flagged as a source to mine further rather than a specific dataset.
